sections.h2: Which offices matter when I sell in Morristown?
sections.html:
Morristown anchors Hamblen County and the Lakeway Area, and two sets of offices touch a sale. City Hall handles city tax and code enforcement, while the county courthouse houses the assessor, the trustee and the Register of Deeds. Some of Morristown extends into Jefferson County, so check which county holds your parcel before making calls.

Census Bureau data show 33,517 people in mid-2025, a rise of 10.2 percent over the 2020 base. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $181,100, which means a few thousand dollars of repairs eats a real slice of the price a house can bring.

sections.h2: Where does Morristown sit and how did it grow?
sections.html:
The city lies in the Tennessee Valley between the Great Smoky Mountains to the south and Clinch Mountain to the north. Cherokee Lake, a TVA reservoir built in the 1940s, is just north of town. Gideon Morris and his brothers received land grants here in 1787, and Morristown was incorporated in 1855 where two stagecoach routes met. The East Tennessee and Virginia Railroad reached it in 1858, and Hamblen County was created in 1870 with Morristown as its seat.

Industry shaped the modern city. The American Enka rayon plant opened in 1947 and closed in 2005, and the city later built three industrial districts, the last near Interstate 81 exit 8. Furniture maker Berkline, which had been in town since 1937, closed in 2011.

sections.h2: Who are the largest Morristown employers?
sections.html:
Morristown is a manufacturing center. A 2021 survey by the area chamber of commerce listed these as the largest employers, and manufacturing is reported to employ about 24 percent of the Hamblen County workforce.

Plant shifts, the school system and the community college provide a base of steady wage earners. The mean commute is 21.5 minutes, per the Census Bureau, so a house close to those job sites saves a worker real driving time.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Morristown homes?
sections.html:
Census Bureau survey figures for 2020 through 2024 point to a modest-priced market:

  • Owners occupy 54.9 percent of homes.
  • Median rent runs $882 a month.
  • Median household income is $47,917.
  • There are 12,282 households averaging 2.52 people.
  • Poverty touches 26.0 percent of residents.
  • The city covers 27.62 square miles of land.

Monthly owner costs are low, a median of $1,177 with a mortgage and $450 without one. A buyer planning to rent the place will weigh your asking price against that $882 rent.

sections.h2: How do East Tennessee seasons affect a Morristown house?
sections.html:
Elevation near 1,300 feet keeps Morristown a little cooler than the warmer parts of Tennessee, though the climate is still humid and subtropical. July highs average 85 degrees, January lows sit near 28, and annual precipitation runs between 44 and 48 inches depending on the record used. Relative humidity averages about 70 percent, and light snow comes occasionally in winter.

That mix of moisture and freeze cycles puts stress on exterior wood, rain gutters, roof flashing and crawl-space vents.

sections.h2: How do Morristown city taxes and Hamblen County taxes work?
sections.html:
The city and the county each send a separate bill. Morristown mails its notices in late September, takes 2 percent off for payment during October, and charges nothing extra if you pay by February 28 of the next year. The City Tax Office is in City Center and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5. A drop box sits in the City Center parking garage, and the office does not accept payment over the phone.

Hamblen County bills real estate through the Trustee, who collects at the courthouse, at the satellite office at 2415 North Davy Crockett Parkway and online at TNPayments.com. The county date to remember is October 1 for the bill and March 1 for delinquency. Call the Trustee at (423) 586-6290 with questions.

One assessment roll serves both governments. The Assessor of Property, in the courthouse at 511 West Second North Street, manages about 32,000 parcels with over $3 billion of appraised value. Houses are assessed at 25 percent of what the assessor appraises them for.

sections.h2: What should a Morristown seller gather first?
sections.html:
Pull these together before offers come in so closing does not wait on paperwork:

  • Your last city tax receipt from the City Tax Office and your Hamblen County receipt from the Trustee.
  • Your deed, which the Register of Deeds can copy from records back to 1860.
  • Any permit paperwork for a roof, furnace, water heater or addition.
  • Notes on any open Codes Enforcement complaint.
  • Names and lease dates for tenants, if any.

Tennessee assessment records reflect ownership as of January 1 of each tax year, so a fall bill can still carry your name after a sale. Settle the split with the buyer in writing.

sections.h2: Can I dispute my Hamblen County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's office, which serves as the contact for the county Board of Equalization. That board hears owners who think the assessed value of land or buildings is wrong. The Comptroller's calendar has county boards convening each June 1, and the State Board deadline is August 1 or 45 days after the county notice, whichever falls later. Ask the Assessor at (423) 586-1852 for this year's filing date.

The buyer receives the next bill, so mention any pending appeal in your conversations.

sections.h2: What Morristown code and permit rules apply to a house I am selling?
sections.html:
Two codes officers look into every complaint, normally within a day. A confirmed violation brings a certified letter and 14 to 21 days to correct it. After that the city may take the owner to City Court, or send a contractor to mow or clean up and attach a lien to the parcel. Have your title agent search for such liens.

A permit is required for a new roof or windows, gas, electrical, plumbing or HVAC work, additions, sheds, carports and pools over 24 inches deep. Building Inspections answers at (423) 585-4626. The common violations are tall grass, junked vehicles, roof holes and unsafe decks. Sleeping in a camper, shed or any structure not built for living is against city rules.

sections.h2: Where does a Hamblen County deed get filed?
sections.html: Hamblen County deeds go to the Register of Deeds, third floor of the Administrative Building at the courthouse, 423-586-6551. Its books reach back to 1860, and it takes in the state's two recordation taxes. On a sale, the realty transfer tax comes to 37 cents per $100 of the higher of price or value, paid by the buyer taking title.

faqs.q: When must Morristown city taxes be paid to avoid penalty?
faqs.a: By February 28 of the year after the bill. Notices arrive at the end of September, and October payers get a 2 percent discount. The office does not take phone payments.

faqs.q: Does Hamblen County send its own tax bill in Morristown?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee collects county tax, which is due October 1 and delinquent March 1. Pay at the courthouse, at the North Davy Crockett Parkway office or through TNPayments.com.

faqs.q: What if Morristown has an open code case on my house?
faqs.a: Fix it or tell the buyer. Codes Enforcement allows 14 to 21 days, and unresolved cases can reach City Court or end in a lien after city cleanup. Call 423-585-1830 to check status.

faqs.q: Where does a Morristown deed get recorded?
faqs.a: With the Hamblen County Register of Deeds, 423-586-6551. If part of your parcel lies in Jefferson County, ask which register applies first.

faqs.q: Which Morristown repairs need a city permit?
faqs.a: New roofs and windows, gas, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work, additions, sheds and pools deeper than 24 inches. Call Building Inspections at (423) 585-4626 before starting.
